sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s demystify how to call methods in Java! Think of methods as little helpers that do specific tasks for you.

• How to invoke (call) a method
• The role of parentheses and semicolons
• Practical examples with `System.out.println()` and `Scanner`

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine methods like vending machines. You press a button (call a method), and it gives you what you want—like a soda or a snack!

In Java, calling a method is just as simple:
• You write the method’s name
• Add parentheses `()` (like pressing the button)
• End with a semicolon `;` (like confirming your choice)

For example, `System.out.println("Hello!")` tells Java to print "Hello!" to the console. The `println` method is like the vending machine’s "print" button.

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Calling a method transfers execution to the method body with the provided arguments
Arguments are the actual values passed to the method; parameters are the variables that receive them
A value-returning method call can be used in expressions and assignments
A void method call is a standalone statement and cannot be used in expressions
The call stack tracks active method invocations and their local variables

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Methods are called with `object.methodName()`. Parentheses `()` and semicolons `;` are non-negotiable. Practice with `println()` and `Scanner` to build confidence. Ready to learn about *return values* next.
